name: Primary Orthostatic Hypotension

criteria.description: Sustained reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing or head-up tilt
Exclusion of secondary causes of orthostatic hypotension such as medication effects, dehydration, or systemic illness
Presence of symptoms attributable to orthostatic hypotension including dizziness, lightheadedness, or syncope upon standing
Autonomic function tests showing impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Sustained blood pressure drop upon standing with exclusion of secondary causes and presence of orthostatic symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary causes and confirmation by autonomic testing when available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension with sustained systolic blood pressure drop ≥20 mmHg
searchTerms: systolic blood pressure drops ≥20 mmHg on standing
significant blood pressure fall when upright
marked low blood pressure on standing
dizziness caused by nerve issues on standing
fatigue related to low blood pressure on standing
head pain related to low blood pressure

occasional.symptomName: Cognitive slowing or difficulty concentrating upon standing

searchTerms: muscle weakness in upper back and neck
feeling sick related to standing up

occasional.symptomName: Cold extremities due to impaired vasoconstriction
searchTerms: cold hands and feet due to poor blood vessel constriction
cold limbs from blood flow issues

rare.symptomName: Visual field defects during orthostatic hypotension episodes
searchTerms: loss of parts of vision during low blood pressure episodes
seeing blind spots during orthostatic hypotension

rare.symptomName: Transient ischemic attacks related to cerebral hypoperfusion
searchTerms: mini strokes from low brain blood flow
brief neurological deficits due to poor cerebral perfusion

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding secondary causes
Possible mild elevation of plasma norepinephrine in supine position
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or shows no specific abnormalities
Cardiac imaging to exclude structural heart disease
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified for primary orthostatic hypotension
other: Autonomic function testing showing impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction
Tilt-table testing confirming orthostatic blood pressure drop

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying systemic illness or medication cause
Reversible with treatment of secondary cause
Syncope triggered by emotional stress or pain
Transient bradycardia and hypotension with prodromal symptoms
Progressive autonomic failure with additional autonomic symptoms

redFlags: Sudden onset of orthostatic hypotension symptoms
Presence of neurological deficits suggesting central nervous system pathology
Recurrent syncope with injury or seizures
references: Freeman R. Clinical practice. Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(6):615-624.
Consensus statement on the definition of orthostatic hypotension, pure autonomic failure, and multiple system atrophy. Neurology. 1996
